subject: Stock own-player status_sv command, console framing, and safe Sleeping/ReceivingSnapshot observation
evidenceKind: Read-only metadata and IL inspection; no command was sent or executed

sources.qualification: This copy has an Oxide IOnServerCommand hook in ConsoleSystem.Internal; its generic permission and reply plumbing are supporting evidence only. Stock command registration and stock game/network handlers were inspected separately.

findings.finding: Registers Name=status_sv, Parent=global, FullName=global.status_sv, ServerUser=true and Variable=false. This entry does not set ServerAdmin. It dispatches to the generated b__2_1502 wrapper.
Passes the same ConsoleSystem.Arg directly to ConVar.Global.status_sv.

Resolves ArgEx.Player(arg), returns if there is no caller player, and replies with that player's GetDebugStatus(). It does not parse a target argument or enumerate other players, and does not call StartSleeping, EndSleeping or a received-tick handler.

Returns null for a null Arg or absent Arg.Connection. Otherwise returns Arg.Connection.player cast to BasePlayer. The selected player is bound to the authenticated game connection, not supplied as a SteamID argument. RCON alone supplies no such player through this helper.

Builds Entity, Name and SteamID lines, then enumerates every PlayerFlags value and appends one '<flag>: <Boolean>\n' line using HasPlayerFlag. It does not read position, eye position, rotation, IP, inventory or authentication tickets. It returns the string without changing any player flag.

The server-side Entity line normally uses a cached display-name-and-user-ID string. It can initialize the formatting cache BaseEntity._name. The output therefore contains account identity even though no coordinates or credentials are read.
These are BasePlayer flags, distinct from BaseEntity.flags and ModelState.flags.

Adds 140 to the enum value for the application byte. A client console command is 0x98; a console reply is 0x97. These are application messages inside the established transport, not standalone UDP datagrams.

The ConsoleCommand branch requires a connected connection, applies maxpacketspersecond_command, and invokes ConsoleNetwork.OnClientCommand. Handler exceptions follow the existing server kick path. No PlayerTick is needed by this branch.

Checks the unread command packet against maxpacketsize_command, reads StringRaw(maxpacketsize_command, false), verifies an existing connected connection, and runs ConsoleSystem with Option.Server.FromConnection(the same connection).Quiet(). Nonempty CommandResult.Output is passed to SendClientReply for that same connection. Quiet suppresses ordinary printed output; it does not discard the command reply.

Raw means UTF-8 text without StringInternal's control-character replacement. It still reads a length prefix. With variableLength=false it reads UInt32, obtains that byte range, and decodes UTF-8; it does not consume an unprefixed remainder string.

The false length-prefix path uses an unmanaged UInt32, with BufferStream reading/writing the native four-byte value. This is little-endian on the inspected Windows x64 runtime. The protocol evidence here must not be generalized to an uninspected big-endian runtime.

Supporting console-library evidence: ServerUser with a non-null connection passes the ordinary permission branch; ReplyWith stores Arg.Reply and RunWithResult exposes it as CommandResult.Output. FromConnection sets the connection and clears FromRcon; Quiet only clears PrintOutput. This library copy also permits an Oxide command hook to intercept execution, so remote plugin behavior remains unverified.

Starts a network write, writes PacketID(ConsoleMessage=11), writes String(output, false), and sends using SendInfo(requestConnection). There is one ordinary string payload, no protobuf field number, command-name echo, entity ID or request-correlation ID in this reply framing.

String encodes UTF-8 and writes the byte count followed by those bytes. variableLength=false selects the fixed UInt32 prefix. The reply preserves the generated newlines in its UTF-8 bytes. SendInfo targets only the provided connection with default method=0, priority=1 and channel=0.

request.direction: Established game client to its server
fields: UTF-8 command byte length as UInt32 little-endian
request.qualification: Accepted layout established from server parsing and shared serializers; no live normal-client request for this command was captured or sent in this task.

reply.direction: Server to the same requesting game connection
fields: UTF-8 output byte length as UInt32 little-endian

preconditions: Use only the already-established own game connection after own-entity and FinishLoading observation.
The only outbound text would be the fixed no-argument global.status_sv constant; do not expose arbitrary console forwarding or a target account parameter.
Allow one pending query with a bounded reply deadline; no PlayerTick, wake command, account reconnect or administrator RPC is involved.
replyValidation: Accept only a ConsoleMessage from the existing connected server while that fixed query is pending.
Require a bounded payload, for example at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes, an exact UInt32 length-to-packet match, and strict UTF-8 decoding.

Validate the complete canonical PlayerFlags suffix from the end of the string, using the ordered names below and exact True/False values; require its final newline and reject missing, duplicate, reordered or extra suffix entries.
Require the exact own SteamID line immediately before that suffix, comparing it privately to the existing logged-in session identity. Never output that line or retain it as public metadata.

Display names can contain untrusted text and newlines. Do not select the first global regex match for Sleeping or ReceivingSnapshot; a forged line in the name/header could otherwise be mistaken for the actual flag tail.
After complete validation retain only the two requested booleans and safe observation count/age; discard the raw text, identity headers and all other flags.
Malformed, unrelated, timed-out or denied replies must keep the previous observation aging, or remain unknown before the first success; they must not become false flags.

fields: sleeping boolean only after a valid reply
receivingSnapshot boolean only after a valid reply
age at the current worker sample

limits: There is no request-correlation ID. One pending request, canonical output and own-identity matching reduce ambiguity but cannot cryptographically bind otherwise identical unsolicited console text to that request.
A different server build, plugin interception or altered output can invalidate the static format; fail unknown instead of guessing.
Reading these flags does not wake the player, prove an EAC session, or establish the reason for any published player-count value.

administratorAlternatives.finding: Supports a substring filter against display name, user ID, owner ID and IP. Normal rows contain id/name/ping/connected/addr/owner/violation/kicks/entityId, with no Sleeping or ReceivingSnapshot. It is not a strict identity-only filter; error/no-connection branches may add rows before filtering. Keep any raw response private and select the exact own identity in memory.

Enumerates the entire sleepingPlayerList and prints all sleeping users' IDs and names, without a target filter. This can establish list membership but does not expose ReceivingSnapshot and is not the minimal private query.

Registered ServerAdmin but the body first dereferences ArgEx.Player for admin/developer/cinematic checks, then reads argument zero using GetUInt (UInt32), converts it to a string and calls FindSleeping before EndSleeping. It is not a verified RCON-with-Steam64 exact-target command; a full Steam64 exceeds the argument type. Do not substitute a truncated numeric ID or assume the generated description proves otherwise.

Registered ServerAdmin. Uses the calling in-game player's eye raycast within five metres, then toggles a non-NPC other player's sleep state. It can call normal EndSleeping for a sleeping looked-at target, but takes no target-account argument and cannot be used from bare RCON. It is a toggle and would instead sleep an already-awake target. No command was executed.
